findings.title: Route-level try/catch asserted by error table but omitted from §5 GET/PUT/DELETE snippets
findings.fix: State explicitly that each of GET/PUT/DELETE wraps its body in try { ... } catch (e) { console.error("[meta-app]", e); return NextResponse.json({ error: "Internal server error" }, { status: 500 }); } so the error-table rows (encrypt throw / DB error -> 500, no secret logged) are realized in code.

findings.title: ENCRYPTION_KEY-missing failure in PUT-create only covered if the handler try/catch exists
findings.fix: Fold into finding 1: ensure the PUT body (including the encrypt() call inside upsert.create) is inside the handler try/catch so a missing ENCRYPTION_KEY surfaces as a generic 500, not a raw throw.

findings.title: §4 step 7 'process exactly as today' does not list the now-dead single-secret webhook lines to delete
findings.fix: Add a note to §4: delete the current `const appSecret = process.env.META_APP_SECRET` guard block and the single-secret ourHex / Buffer.from(ourHex) compare entirely; they are fully replaced by steps 2-6. Only `const raw`, the theirHex/`a` extraction (step 2), and the processing loop (step 7) survive from the original body.
